dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です。今日はどんなお話をなさりたいですか？
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm a counselor. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 家族のことについてです。
dialogue.English: It's about my family.

dialogue.content: ご家族の事なんですね、お話お聞きいたします。相談中のお名前、ご年齢、性別をできる範囲で教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: I see, it's about your family. I'm here to listen. May I ask for your name, age, and gender for this consultation, to the extent you're comfortable sharing?

dialogue.content: 4代女性です。Kと呼んでください
dialogue.English: I'm a woman in my 40s. Please call me K.

dialogue.content: Ｋさん、ありがとうございます。どんなご家族のお悩みでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you, K. What kind of concerns do you have about your family?

dialogue.content: 夫と子ども二人家族です。子どもは成人しています。
dialogue.English: It's me, my husband, and our two children. The children are adults now.

dialogue.content: そうですか、お子様は社会人になられているんですね
dialogue.English: I see, your children have become working adults, haven't they?

dialogue.content: 夫との会話が成立しないというか・・・話しがいがないというか
dialogue.English: It's like I can't have a proper conversation with my husband… or that it feels pointless to talk to him.

dialogue.content: 話してて楽しくないというか
dialogue.English: Or that it's just not enjoyable to talk to him.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: それは、お寂しい気持がなさいますね
dialogue.English: That must feel lonely.

dialogue.content: 寂しいというか、会話に意味を感じなくて
dialogue.English: It's not so much loneliness, but more that I don't feel any meaning in our conversations.

dialogue.content: 「意味のある会話」が無いとお感じなんですね、夫さんも同じくらいのご年齢ですか？
dialogue.English: So you feel there are no 'meaningful conversations'. Is your husband around the same age as you?

dialogue.content: 8つ上です
dialogue.English: He's eight years older.

dialogue.content: すると・・・50代半ばというところでしょうか。お仕事はなさっていますよね
dialogue.English: So... that would put him in his mid-fifties, perhaps. He is working, correct?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 会話が味気なく感じられるという事は、お子様が育った今となっては先への不安にもつながっておられるのでしょうか
dialogue.English: Feeling that your conversations are so bland—now that your children are grown, does that also connect to anxiety about the future?

dialogue.content: 私も仕事をしていますが、話したいというよりも、話したことをちゃんと覚えれほしいのですが
dialogue.English: I work as well, but more than wanting to talk, I wish he would properly remember what I've told him.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 先への不安はないです。
dialogue.English: I don't have any anxiety about the future.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Understood.

dialogue.content: ”あれ　ふとった？”とか本当にいみないのですよね
dialogue.English: Things like, 'Oh, have you gained weight?' are just so meaningless, you know?

dialogue.content: そうなんですね・・・。表面的な会話になってしまうのですね
dialogue.English: I see... The conversations become superficial, don't they?

dialogue.content: これがずっと続くのかと思うと嫌になる。
dialogue.English: Thinking that this will go on forever makes me fed up.

dialogue.content: なるほど、いつごろからご夫婦の会話に意味が無いとお感じですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Since about when have you felt that your conversations with your husband are meaningless?

dialogue.content: 趣味も合わないし、興味も違うし、今までは子育てで、共通の課題があったものの、ないのですよね。意味が
dialogue.English: Our hobbies don't align, our interests are different, and while we used to have the common goal of raising children, we don't have that anymore. There's no meaning.

dialogue.content: 子育てという共通の課題が無くなったことが会話を無意味にさせたのかもしれないとお感じなのですね。
dialogue.English: So you feel that losing the common goal of raising children may have made your conversations feel meaningless.

dialogue.content: Ｋさんにとって夫さんとの生活の理想の形はどんなものだと思われますか？
dialogue.English: For you, K, what would an ideal life with your husband look like?

dialogue.content: そうですね。会話の必要性がないというか…一日の業務連絡が終わればいいっかという感じです。
dialogue.English: Well... it feels like there's almost no need for conversation. As long as we get the day's logistics handled, that's good enough.

dialogue.content: 連絡事項だけでは、さみしいですよね。。。
dialogue.English: Just dealing with logistical matters would be lonely, wouldn't it...

dialogue.content: 理想ですか？　自分が興味あることを話したときに、入りすぎず、茶化さない。ですかね。
dialogue.English: My ideal? When I talk about something I'm interested in, for him not to get too involved and not to make fun of it. I guess that's it.

dialogue.content: 寂しいというより、茶化されたり、上から目線が嫌です。
dialogue.English: It's less about feeling lonely, and more that I hate being teased or talked down to.

dialogue.content: なるほど、Ｋさんの話したい事をもう少し真摯に聴いて欲しいというお気持ちは当然だと思います。自分の毎日を茶化されたり上から批評されるのはたまらない気持になりますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. It's completely natural to want him to listen more sincerely to what you have to say. It must be unbearable to have your daily life mocked or criticized in a condescending way.

dialogue.content: そうですね。真摯というほど、丁寧でなくていいので、そうなんだねくらいでいいのです。仕事の分野が全く違うので、わかったように言われるのも腹が立つので。
dialogue.English: That's right. It doesn't have to be as 'sincere' as all that; a simple 'Oh, I see' would be enough. Our fields of work are completely different, so it's irritating when he acts like he understands everything.

dialogue.content: まあお互いだとは思うのですが。
dialogue.English: Although, I suppose it goes both ways.

dialogue.content: それはそうですよね、全部を分かっているように言われたら、私もカチンと来てしまいそうです。
dialogue.English: That makes sense. If someone acted like they understood everything, I think I would get a little annoyed too.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。その一言はちょっとうれしい！
dialogue.English: Thank you. Hearing you say that makes me a little happy!

dialogue.content: 誰でも感じる気持ちだと思います！（笑）
dialogue.English: I think anyone would feel that way! (laughs)

dialogue.content: お互い様と言うと、Ｋさんもそんな態度になってしまう事があるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: When you say 'it goes both ways,' does that mean you sometimes find yourself acting that way too?

dialogue.content: あまり、真剣には聞いていないです。
dialogue.English: I don't listen to him very seriously either.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、お互い外から帰ってお疲れの時はそんな気持ちになってしまいますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. It's natural to feel that way when you're both tired after coming home from work.

dialogue.content: でも、茶化さないようにはしています。
dialogue.English: But I do try not to make fun of him.

dialogue.content: それは立派な事だと思います！
dialogue.English: I think that's admirable!

dialogue.content: 長い付き合いの中で、「気心が知れた」とも言いますが気づかいがなかなかできなくなることはたくさんあると思いますが、気を付けていらっしゃるんですね！
dialogue.English: In a long relationship, people say you 'know each other inside and out,' and I think it often becomes difficult to be considerate, but it sounds like you're making a conscious effort!

dialogue.content: というか、茶かすと不機嫌になるので、めんどくさい。
dialogue.English: Well, it's more that if I tease him he gets grumpy, and it's a hassle.

dialogue.content: 正解だとおもいます！（笑）
dialogue.English: I think that's the right way to handle it! (laughs)

dialogue.content: ちっとも立派でも、愛情深いわけでもありません。平和ならいいのです。
dialogue.English: It's not admirable or affectionate at all. As long as there's peace, that's all that matters.

dialogue.content: 私の望みは、平和な一日　です。
dialogue.English: My wish is for a peaceful day.

dialogue.content: 茶化されても、聞き流していたのですが、これでは平和な一日にならないと思い反論することにしました。
dialogue.English: I used to just let his teasing slide, but I realized that wouldn't lead to a peaceful day, so I decided to start pushing back.

dialogue.content: 平和な一日！大切ですよね！でも、それが崩れてしまうのが夫さんの「茶化し」や「上から目線」なのですよね。ここまでのお話を聞いていて何とか夫さんとの平和な時間が作れてＫさんが少しでも気持ちを軽く出来ないかと考えています。
dialogue.English: A peaceful day! That's so important, isn't it? But it's your husband's 'teasing' and 'condescending attitude' that shatters it. Listening to you, I've been thinking about how we can create some peaceful time with your husband so that you can feel even a little bit lighter.

dialogue.content: 反論するとどんな風になりますか？
dialogue.English: What happens when you push back?

dialogue.content: 不機嫌になり、喧嘩のようになります。このバトルが…いつまで続くのかが本当の悩みかなそろそろ私が嫌がっていることに気が付いてほしいのですが、
dialogue.English: He gets upset, and it turns into something like a fight. This battle... I guess my real worry is how long it will last. I wish he would realize by now that I don't like it.

dialogue.content: そうですよね・・・。喧嘩のようになると、そもそも伝えたかったことが伝わらなくなるでしょうね。疲れてしまいますよね。。。
dialogue.English: That's right... When it turns into a fight, what you originally wanted to convey doesn't get through, does it? It's exhausting...

dialogue.content: 年齢を重ねると　平和が一番で。でも、今伝えないと老後ずっとになると嫌なので。
dialogue.English: As I get older, peace is the most important thing. But if I don't say something now, I hate the idea of it continuing like this into our old age.

dialogue.content: 今まではめんどくさいから、ほかってきてたので。今戦っています。
dialogue.English: Until now, I've just let it go because it was a hassle. Now, I'm fighting.

dialogue.content: 素晴らしいです！その通りですよね、夫さんとのこれからをより良い時間にしていくことをご一緒に考えてみましょう！
dialogue.English: That's wonderful! You're absolutely right. Let's think together about how to make your future time with your husband better!

dialogue.content: はい。平和な時間になるようにお願いします。
dialogue.English: Yes. Please help me find a way to have more peaceful times.

dialogue.content: 茶化してしまう人の心理って、一般的には「ウケ狙いで話の腰を折る」や「会話に照れている」などの原因があるように思うのですが、夫さんはどうして茶化してしまうのだと思われますか？
dialogue.English: Generally, the psychology of people who tease is often attributed to things like 'interrupting the conversation to get a laugh' or 'being embarrassed by the conversation.' Why do you think your husband teases you?

dialogue.content: 私の思いがわかっていない。なんか昭和の笑いみたいだなあと思います。茶化しが愛情表現みたいな。
dialogue.English: He doesn't understand my feelings. I think it's like an old-fashioned, Showa-era kind of humor, where teasing is a form of affection.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね！「かまってちゃん」なのかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: I see! He might be a bit of an attention-seeker.

dialogue.content: なので、仕方ない　平和な老後のために　嫌なものは嫌だと　伝えていこうと思うのですが、結構疲れます。
dialogue.English: So, I feel like I have no choice. For the sake of a peaceful old age, I'm trying to keep telling him that I don't like what I don't like, but it's quite tiring.

dialogue.content: 当然のお気持ちだと思います、Ｋさんのイライラ来る気持ちはわかっていただかなければと、私も思います！
dialogue.English: I think it's perfectly natural to feel that way. I also believe he needs to understand how frustrating this is for you!

dialogue.content: なんか、良い伝え方がありますかね？
dialogue.English: Is there, you know, a good way to tell him?

dialogue.content: Ｋさんと夫さんはお話合いの時間をお取りになれそうでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Do you think you and your husband could set aside some time to talk things over?

dialogue.content: 日常の中で訓練したいです。向き合って話すと、喧嘩になります。
dialogue.English: I'd like to practice it in our daily life. If we sit down to talk face-to-face, it just turns into a fight.

dialogue.content: そんなにかしこまる訳ではないのですが、ルール作りをしてみてはいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: It wouldn't have to be so formal, but how about creating some rules?

dialogue.content: ん？
dialogue.English: Hmm?

dialogue.content: 「茶化される事が嫌」と言う事を伝えた上で、
dialogue.English: After you've told him that you don't like being teased,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 茶化したら「お風呂掃除！」とか、Ｋさんも適当に受け流してしまったら、夫さんに「肩モミ！」とか
dialogue.English: if he teases you, the penalty is 'you have to clean the bathroom!' Or if you just brush off something he says, your penalty is 'you have to give him a shoulder massage!'

dialogue.content: ちょっと笑えるルールを作れたら、気軽に毎日の中で軽く嫌な気持ちがすることを伝えあえると思うのです。
dialogue.English: If you can make some light-hearted rules, I think you'll be able to casually communicate to each other about the little things that bother you in your daily life.

dialogue.content: 楽しそうですね。ありがとうございます。が、今の私はそれは余計に喜んでじゃれているように受け取られそうです。
dialogue.English: That sounds fun, thank you. But, the way things are now, he's likely to take that as me just happily playing along.

dialogue.content: 最初に「イヤ」と言う事をお伝えになることが難しそうですか？
dialogue.English: Does it seem difficult to first tell him that you don't like it?

dialogue.content: なるほど、喜んでいると思われたらもっと茶化されてしまいますね。
dialogue.English: I see. If he thinks you're enjoying it, he'll just tease you more, won't he?

dialogue.content: 嫌！のソフトなしかし明確な強さをもって伝えたいと思っています。
dialogue.English: I want to convey that I don't like it in a way that's soft, yet clearly firm.

dialogue.content: そうですね、まずは伝えることが出来るのは私も大切だと思います。
dialogue.English: Right, I agree that being able to communicate that first is very important.

dialogue.content: 嫌！の五段階活用みたいな。
dialogue.English: Like, five levels of intensity for saying 'I don't like it!'

dialogue.content: 2つほど案があるのですが
dialogue.English: I have a couple of ideas, if you'd like to hear them.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: もし、会話で伝えられるなら、家庭を離れてカフェや公園など、オープンな場所で話してみるのもいいと思います。特別に時間を作って話すことで、夫さんに真剣さが伝わると思います。
dialogue.English: If you think you can convey it through conversation, I think it might be a good idea to talk in a public place away from home, like a cafe or a park. By setting aside special time to talk, I think he'll understand your seriousness.

dialogue.content: なるほど。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 会話は喧嘩につながりそうで不安でしたら、お手紙はいかがでしょう。
dialogue.English: If you're anxious that a conversation might lead to a fight, how about a letter?

dialogue.content: 文字は、残るので・・・。
dialogue.English: But written words are permanent...

dialogue.content: お手紙は後まで残るので、やはり真剣さが伝わると思うのです。
dialogue.English: That's true, and because a letter remains, I think it's a good way to convey seriousness.

dialogue.content: そうなんですよね、私もどちらかというと会話が良いかなと
dialogue.English: That's true. I also tend to think a conversation would be better.

dialogue.content: 夫さんは弁が立つ方で、きっと頭も良い方なので、遠回りな事はお嫌いかもと思いました。
dialogue.English: Your husband seems articulate and is probably quite smart, so I thought he might not like indirect approaches.

dialogue.content: 家ではないところで、さりげなく伝えるということですね。夫と私は二人で”温泉同好会”なので伝えてみます。伝えた後寝たふりをして様子を見ます。
dialogue.English: So, bring it up casually in a place that isn't home. My husband and I have our own little two-person 'Hot Springs Club,' so I'll try telling him then. After I say it, I'll pretend to be asleep and see how he reacts.

dialogue.content: 日頃の空間でないところだと、少し客観的になれるかもしれませんね。温泉同好会！素敵ですね！
dialogue.English: Being in a space that's different from your usual environment might help you both be a bit more objective. A Hot Springs Club! That's wonderful!

dialogue.content: 唯一　残ってる？つながりです（笑）
dialogue.English: It's the only connection we have left... maybe? (laughs)

dialogue.content: とても素晴らしいつながりですよ！きっといままで流してくれていたＫさんが、改めて話してくれたことは、夫さんの気持ちに響くと思います！
dialogue.English: That's a very wonderful connection! I'm sure the fact that you, who have always let things slide until now, are bringing this up again seriously will resonate with him!

dialogue.content: もしこのチャレンジに失敗したら、また相談に乗てくださいませ。
dialogue.English: If this challenge fails, please allow me to consult with you again.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: でも、長年の癖でもあると思うので、少し長い目でチャレンジいたしましょう！
dialogue.English: But this is likely a long-standing habit of his, so let's approach this challenge with a long-term perspective!

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: You're right.

dialogue.content: また成果など聞かせてください！
dialogue.English: Please let me know how it goes!

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: I will.

dialogue.content: そろそろ時間となってしまいますが、話足りないことなどありませんか？
dialogue.English: Our time is almost up, but is there anything else you feel you haven't had a chance to say?

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です。ありがとうございました。すっきりしました。
dialogue.English: No, I'm okay. Thank you very much. I feel much better.

dialogue.content: 良かったです！それでは「温泉チャレンジ作戦」の成功をお祈りしております。また何かお困りになったらご相談にいらしてください。
dialogue.English: I'm glad to hear that! Well then, I'll be rooting for the success of 'Operation Hot Spring Challenge.' Please feel free to come and talk with me again if anything else comes up.

dialogue.content: 本日はありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your time today.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: （ロープレありがとうございました。勉強になりました！）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for the role-play. It was a great learning experience!)

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well.

dialogue.content: （失礼いたします）
dialogue.English: (If you'll excuse me.)

dialogue.content: 失礼します。
dialogue.English: Goodbye.
